samples.question: Exactly one stroke in this picture is a long unbroken wire: it winds inward as a rectangular spiral of straight runs and square corners, and it covers the whole page from the outer border to the middle. One end of the wire carries a small filled round bead just inside its tip; the other end is a bare tip. At twenty-five places along the wire, spread over every part of the spiral, the wire briefly leaves its lane: it steps sideways by a short jog, runs a short distance parallel to the lane it left, and steps back into that same lane. There are exactly twenty-five such detours and nothing else interrupts the wire. Carry out this operation: stand at the beaded end facing along the wire, walk the wire all the way to the bare tip, and for each detour in the order you meet it record whether the wire stepped out to your left hand or to your right hand at that moment, judging left and right from the direction you are walking at that point, not from the page. Write those twenty-five records into a 5 by 5 grid in that same order, filling row 1 left to right, then row 2, and so on to row 5, and mark every grid cell whose detour went to your left. Exactly 9 of the 25 cells are marked. The marked cells form one symbol on the grid: 'tee' is the whole top row together with the centre column below it; 'ell' is the whole left column together with the bottom row; 'plus' is the whole centre row together with the whole centre column; 'ex' is the two full diagonals. The spiral's winding sense, which tip carries the bead, the colours, the wire's position on the page and the small scattered squares elsewhere are decoration; only the left-or-right handedness of the twenty-five detours, taken in walking order from the beaded end, decides the symbol. Which symbol do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tee.
